speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are here regarding a dermatological condition with potential oncologic implications; to begin my evaluation, have you noticed any new moles or skin lesions changing in size, shape, or color recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (SCC) of the penis and left middle finger. The presentation of non-healing, red, crusty lesions in a 62-year-old male with a heavy smoking history and recent immigration from a region with high UV exposure strongly supports this diagnosis, likely representing multifocal SCC.
